widgets_values:
For the target video, <Picture 1> (Harry's four-view turnaround), <Picture 2> (Draco's four-view turnaround) and <Picture 3> (the Hogwarts great hall interior) are referenced throughout as character and setting references, not as keyframes.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] 2D-animated, cel-shaded Japanese TV anime style. Inside the Hogwarts great hall from <Picture 3> at breakfast: four long house tables crowded with plates and goblets, lit candles floating overhead, warm morning light slanting through the tall windows. Draco from <Picture 2> — a proud girl with waist-length platinum-blonde hair, grey-blue eyes and red lips, wearing her Slytherin uniform with a grey pleated skirt and glossy black tights — carries a breakfast tray and walks down the central aisle from frame-left toward frame-right; the camera trucks right at slow speed alongside her. Students at the tables turn their heads to watch her pass. [Shot 2] At 00:02.500, the camera cuts to a static medium shot across the Gryffindor table. Harry from <Picture 1> — a tall boy with messy black hair, green eyes, round glasses and a lightning scar on his forehead, wearing his Gryffindor uniform — sits on the bench at frame-right, facing the camera across the table. Draco enters from frame-left, swings her robe aside, and sits down on the bench right beside him at frame-center; her tray lands on the table with a thud. Harry looks up at her. [Shot 3] At 00:05.000, the camera cuts to a close shot of the two of them and pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed. Draco, at frame-left, casually picks up the goblet of pumpkin juice in front of Harry at frame-right, takes a sip, sets it down, and raises one eyebrow at him; Harry blinks once, caught off guard. [Shot 4] At 00:07.500, the camera cuts to a static close-up. Harry breaks into a smile and slides his own plate to the middle of the table between them; Draco presses her lips together but her smile escapes, the tips of her ears turn red, and she turns her face away toward frame-left.

overall_soundscape: A bustling breakfast-hall ambience of students chatting, with clinking cutlery and plates throughout. A wooden tray thuds onto the table, a metal goblet is lifted and set back down, and a soft boyish laugh sounds near the end as the surrounding chatter warms back up.

non_diegetic_music: A light, playful arrangement of pizzicato strings and flute at a moderate waltz tempo runs throughout, with a gentle swell of warm strings in the final three seconds.

widgets_values:
参数	默认	说明
context_latent	—	上一镜的 AV latent，直接来自 H3 Motion Context Load Latent。
tail_frames	"22"	注入的像素帧数，会换算成潜变量步。只有 5 / 22 / 39 / 56 是整步数（→ 2 / 7 / 12 / 17 步）。建议与 H3 Motion Context 的 context_length 保持一致。
alpha	0.45	窗口内平坦注入强度。
alpha_end	0.10	最末帧强度，必须 ≤ alpha。
ramp_steps	2	末尾降噪的潜变量步数（一步约等于 4 像素帧，2 步约等于像素配方里的 3 帧斜坡）。
seed	0	高斯噪声种子。
noise_scale	match_latent_std	match_latent_std 让高斯按被携带窗口自身的标准差缩放，alpha 的含义与 latent 尺度无关；unit 使用原始 N(0,1)。

widgets_values:
H3 MOTION CONTEXT + REFERENCE MODE - QUICK START

Same chaining as the T2V setup, with reference images, video or audio
steering the look. Your references are kept and the continuation audio
is added alongside them. Nothing to configure for that.

Needs H3 Motion Context from August 2026 or later. Older versions
refused to run reference mode and chaining together.

WIRING:
MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo -> H3 Motion Context -> guider / sampler
References go on the reference node as usual. Motion Context sits after
it and leaves them alone.

FIRST CLIP OF A CHAIN:
- Mute/bypass the H3 Motion Context group
- Set Save Latent clip_index to 1 and generate as normal
  (the workflow ships wired for clip 2: Load = 1, Save = 2)

EVERY CLIP AFTER THAT:
- Unmute everything
- Load Latent clip_index = the clip to CONTINUE FROM
- Save Latent clip_index = the clip you are making NOW
- Keep the same references wired as the previous clip

Retry and index handling are identical to the T2V note above.

SETTINGS THAT WORK (tested):
context_length "22", audio_context_length 24.
24 frames is exactly one second of sound, and any
multiple of 3 lands exactly on the audio grid.

PROMPTING IS THE HARD PART HERE. Read this bit.

The pinned frames are not a suggestion. They are re-injected at every
sampling step and the model cannot render anything else in that span.
So if the prompt for clip 2 opens describing something different from
how clip 1 ended, the model does not choose between them - it renders
BOTH. Clip 1 ends on a close-up of one character, clip 2 opens asking
for a two-shot of two others, and you get three people in the frame.

The fix: open every prompt by describing how the PREVIOUS clip ended.
Same person, same clothes, same framing, same action. Let that run for
a beat past the join, then change to whatever you actually want. The
pinned frames get a stretch of timeline that agrees with them, and the
change happens where nothing is pinned.

Give the hold something to do - a breath, a weight shift, an eyeline
change. A held framing with nothing happening in it renders as a frozen
frame and looks like the video stalled.

At 22 frames of context the pin is 0.92s, and you want a beat past that,
so plan on the change landing around 1.5 to 2 seconds in. On a 5 second
clip that is most of the first half. Longer clips are easier than a
shorter hold.

REFERENCES HAVE NO TIMING. Every reference conditions the whole clip.
There is no way to say "this one applies from two seconds in." If the
outfit, location or character changes partway through, the shot
structure and the description have to carry that on their own.

Dark Blue Headers: H3 Motion Context nodes
Green Headers: nodes that need a user input between clips
